filename: Accurate and Efficient Hybrid-Ensemble Atmospheric Data Assimilation in Latent Space with Uncertainty Quantification.pdf
title: Accurate and Efficient Hybrid-Ensemble Atmospheric Data Assimilation in Latent Space with Uncertainty Quantification
code_availability: Codes and model checkpoints used in this study will be available at https://github.com/hangfan99/HLOBA at time of publication.
testbed_rationale: Focuses on developing a latent space data assimilation framework (HLOBA) for weather forecasting rather than generating or hosting a parameterization testbed dataset.
pain_points: High computational and memory demands of 4D variational and ensemble data assimilation scaling with resolution and observation volume
Accurate uncertainty quantification in high-dimensional model space is hindered by small ensemble sizes, leading to sampling noise and spurious correlations
Deterministic ML forecast models are insensitive to initial-condition perturbations, yielding poorly spread perturbation-based ensembles
Indirect observation operators (e.g., satellite radiances) require substantial implementation overhead for O2Lnet training
Need for differentiable forecast models and observation operators in standard L4DVar and 4DVar, which incurs heavy optimization and memory overhead
extraction_notes: The forecast model used in cycling DA is FengWu (a data-driven global weather forecasting model), retrained with latent-space loss constraints. The date on the arXiv preprint is March 4, 2026.
